issues.legal_issue: An appeal challenging cancellation of sub-leases becomes academic when the sub-leases have expired, except where the effect of the consent remains unresolved.
material_facts: The sub-leases in the appeals had expired by the time the Supreme Court considered them, making the requested relief concerning their cancellation academic.
For one sub-lessee, the record did not establish whether the consent to sub-lease had been given before or after a change in the applicable requirements.
issues.conclusion: The first set of appeals was disposed of as infructuous, except for the case in which the Government was directed to determine when consent had been given.
issues.legal_principle: A court need not decide an appeal where expiry of the relevant lease has made the requested relief academic. Where the record leaves an issue material to the continuing effect of a sub-lease unresolved, that issue may require determination rather than disposal as academic.

rule.if: appeal_challenging_sublease_cancellation and subleases_expired and not consent_timing_unresolved

predicates.appeal_challenging_sublease_cancellation: The proceeding is an appeal challenging the cancellation of sub-leases.
predicates.subleases_expired: The sub-leases at issue have expired before the appeal is decided.
predicates.consent_timing_unresolved: The record does not establish whether consent was given before or after a change in the applicable requirements.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges sub-lease cancellations and the sub-leases have expired, the appeal is infructuous if the timing of consent raises no unresolved issue.

issues.legal_issue: The requirement for prior central approval introduced by the amended sub-leasing rule does not invalidate sub-leases made before that requirement took effect.
material_facts: The relevant consents and sub-leases, apart from one case separately considered, predated the change that imposed a requirement for prior central approval.
The Government and the Corporation argued that the sub-leases were void for want of that approval.
issues.conclusion: The prior-approval requirement did not apply to the sub-leases made before the amendment, and the argument that those sub-leases were void ab initio was rejected.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied Rule 37 of the Mineral Concession Rules, 1960, as amended, and Section 4A of the Mines and Minerals (Regulation and Development) Act, 1957. It held that the amended Rule 37 requirement for prior central approval did not govern sub-leases made before the amendment took effect; it also observed that Section 4A's restriction on grant of a mining lease without central approval applied to the State Government, not to the Corporation that had already been granted a lease.

predicates.sublease_validity_appeal: The proceeding challenges the validity of a sub-lease on the ground that prior central approval was absent.
predicates.consent_preceded_new_approval_requiremen: Consent to the sub-lease was given before the requirement for prior central approval took effect.

issues.definition: If a validity appeal concerns a sub-lease and consent preceded the new approval requirement, central approval is not required for that sub-lease.

issues.legal_issue: A contractual dispute is reviewable under Article 226 when the challenged action involves exercise of statutory power and breach of a statutory obligation.
material_facts: The Government withdrew consent and the Corporation cancelled sub-leases under a statutory framework governing mining leases and sub-leases.
The challenged action was alleged to have violated statutory requirements and was not merely a private contractual decision.
issues.conclusion: The dispute did not arise purely in the contractual field, and the High Court could consider it under Article 226.
issues.legal_principle: Where a breach of contract also involves breach of a statutory obligation and the challenged order is made in exercise of statutory power, the matter enters the sphere of public law. Government action in contracting remains subject to reasonableness, fair play and public interest. The Court relied on M/s Dwarkadas Marfatia & Sons v. Board of Trustees of the Port of Bombay, Mahabir Auto Stores v. Indian Oil Corporation, and Srilekha Vidyarthi v. State of U.P., and distinguished the earlier line represented by Radhakrishna Agarwal v. State of Bihar.

predicates.article_226_contractual_proceeding: The proceeding seeks judicial review of government or agency action connected with a contract.
predicates.challenged_action_exercises_statutory_po: The challenged action was taken by an authority exercising statutory power.
predicates.alleged_statutory_breach: The claimant alleges that the action breached a statutory obligation or governing legal requirement.

issues.definition: A contractual dispute is reviewable under Article 226 when the proceeding challenges action taken under statutory power and alleges breach of a statutory obligation.

issues.legal_issue: A court should not extend an expired mining sub-lease to compensate for a period of interrupted operations when extension would be impractical, contrary to government policy, or harmful to the public interest.
material_facts: The sub-lessees sought additional time to conduct mining operations for periods during which they had been prevented from operating.
The sub-leases had expired years before the Supreme Court's decision, and restarting operations would require renewed infrastructure and logistical arrangements for a short period.
The Government's policy was not to grant leases or sub-leases to private parties, and a House Committee had identified alleged malpractices whose continuation could harm the public interest.
issues.conclusion: The High Court should not have extended the expired sub-leases, and the order granting that relief was set aside.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied the discretionary approach to specific performance discussed in Kalyanpur Lime Works Ltd. v. State of Bihar, AIR 1954 SC 165. It held that extension was inappropriate in light of the elapsed time, practical difficulties, the Government's policy, and the public interest.

rule.if: proceeding_seeking_extension_of_expired_sublease and lease_term_expired and (extension_impractical or extension_conflicts_with_policy or extension_perpetuates_public_harm)

predicates.proceeding_seeking_extension_of_expired_: The proceeding seeks additional operating time under an expired sub-lease as compensation for an interruption.
predicates.lease_term_expired: The term of the sub-lease has expired before the court decides whether to extend it.
predicates.extension_impractical: Resuming operations would require substantial renewed infrastructure or logistical arrangements for only a short period.
predicates.extension_conflicts_with_policy: The proposed extension conflicts with the government's policy on granting leases or sub-leases.
predicates.extension_perpetuates_public_harm: The extension would perpetuate practices identified as harmful to the public interest.

issues.definition: A court should not extend an expired sub-lease sought as compensation for interrupted operations when extension is impractical, conflicts with policy, or would perpetuate public harm.

issues.legal_issue: A claim for damages arising from alleged wrongful cancellation or interruption of a sub-lease should be pursued in a civil suit, with its cause of action reckoned from the final determination of the parties' rights.
material_facts: The sub-lessees alleged that wrongful cancellation and interruption of mining operations caused them loss.
The High Court granted additional operating time rather than deciding the damages claim.
The Supreme Court declined to decide whether a contractual breach entitled the sub-lessees to damages.
issues.conclusion: The parties may pursue their respective claims in civil suits; the Supreme Court left entitlement to damages open and directed that the cause of action be reckoned from the date of its order.
issues.legal_principle: The Court distinguished restitution by extending a lease from the separate question whether breach of contract gives rise to damages. It left the latter question for determination in civil proceedings, uninfluenced by the High Court's observations or findings on that aspect.

predicates.proceeding_involving_damages_claim: The proceeding includes a claim for damages arising from the handling of a contractual relationship.
predicates.alleged_contractual_loss: A party alleges loss caused by wrongful cancellation or interruption of contractual performance.
predicates.damages_entitlement_not_decided: The court has not decided whether the alleged breach entitles the claimant to damages.

issues.definition: When a proceeding includes an alleged contractual loss but does not decide entitlement to damages, the claim may be pursued in a civil suit.

issues.legal_issue: Where the effect of a sub-lease depends on whether consent was given before or after a new approval requirement took effect, the Government must determine when consent was given.
material_facts: A sub-lessee obtained a sub-lease, but the record did not show whether it relied on earlier general consent or on separate consent.
The sub-lease's effect depended on whether consent preceded or followed the introduction of a requirement for prior central approval.
issues.conclusion: The Government was directed to determine whether consent had been given before or after the new requirement took effect; the sub-lease might be affected if consent was later and might not be affected if consent was earlier.
issues.legal_principle: Under Rule 37 of the Mineral Concession Rules, 1960, as amended, the requirement for prior approval applied from the amendment's effective date. The Court therefore made the effect of the sub-lease turn on when consent had been given.

predicates.proceeding_concerning_sublease_validity: The proceeding concerns whether a sub-lease remains legally effective.
predicates.consent_timing_uncertain: The record does not establish when the relevant consent was given.
predicates.sublease_effect_depends_on_timing: The sub-lease's legal effect depends on whether consent preceded a new approval requirement.

issues.definition: When a sub-lease validity proceeding turns on uncertain consent timing, the Government must determine when consent was given.
